payload.title: How Do You Get a Marriage Licence?
payload.meta_title: Marriage Licence in Australia and How It Works Overseas
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: An engaged Australian couple in their 30s with a budget of AUD 150k or more, planning a destination wedding, who have searched 'marriage licence' expecting to apply for one and need to learn quickly that Australia issues none, what the equivalent step is (the Notice of Intended Marriage to an authorised celebrant), how a licence differs from the marriage certificate, how licences work if they marry legally in places such as New Zealand or Hawaii, and which country to make the wedding legal in, so they can choose a path and get back to planning the celebration.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor: request a Wedded Concierge consultation at /wonderland-concierge so an Advisor can plan the venue, travel, vendors and payments for the wedding abroad (the licence, NOIM and all legal steps stay with the couple, their authorised celebrant and the relevant authorities).
payload.angle: Page-one results for 'marriage licence' are mostly US county clerk pages and generic explainers that assume every couple applies for a licence. This guide starts from what an Australian couple actually needs to hear: Australia issues no marriage licence; the equivalent step is giving a Notice of Intended Marriage to an authorised celebrant within the legal window, then marrying and registering with the state registry. It summarises that briefly and sends readers to our NOIM guide for detail, explains the licence versus certificate difference as official sources state it, shows how licences work where they do exist (New Zealand through Births, Deaths and Marriages, Hawaii through the State Department of Health) reused from our country guides, and closes with the real decision for a destination couple: marry legally in Australia and celebrate abroad, or marry legally abroad. General information as at November 2026, not legal advice.
must_include: Intro with a direct answer in the first 100 words: Australia issues no marriage licence; you give a Notice of Intended Marriage to an authorised celebrant within the window the Attorney-General's Department states, then marry and the marriage is registered; dated 'as at November 2026' and framed as general information, not legal advice. Then exactly 4 Key takeaways, one sentence each: (1) no licence in Australia, the NOIM to an authorised celebrant is the equivalent step; (2) a licence permits a marriage while a certificate records one, as official sources state; (3) countries such as New Zealand and Hawaii issue licences through their own authorities; (4) the key choice is which country makes the marriage legal.

Section 'What Replaces a Licence in Australia' (summary only): the NOIM window, the authorised celebrant, the legal words and the certificate and registration with the state registry, each reused from the NOIM, who-can-perform and ceremony script packs (AGD; Marriage Act 1961 s45 and s46 via AustLII) and linked at the claim. Prominent link to /expert-advice/notice-of-intended-marriage (draft: link if live at publish, otherwise a LINK comment) and /expert-advice/who-can-perform-a-marriage. No timing figures restated beyond what the NOIM pack sourced; legal words quoted as the Act's text only.

Section 'Marriage Licence and Marriage Certificate': the difference as the official sources state it, from the ml_a re-check (AGD marriage page plus one state registry page on certificates, for example NSW BDM), only as stated. One line that the certificate is needed for a name change, linking /expert-advice/name-change-after-marriage (draft: link if live, else LINK comment). No registry fees.

Section 'How Marriage Licences Work Overseas': New Zealand (licence from Births, Deaths and Marriages) and Hawaii (licence from the State Department of Health) reused from those packs with the same sources and dates, summarised, linking /destination-weddings/get-married-in-new-zealand and /destination-weddings/getting-married-in-hawaii. Other countries: 'ask the destination's authorities' plus the Smartraveller marrying-overseas line. Recognition in Australia from the AGD fact reused from the symbolic ceremony and Punta Cana packs, linked at the claim.

Section 'Choosing Where to Marry Legally': legal in Australia then a symbolic ceremony abroad, or legal abroad under local rules. Link /expert-advice/symbolic-ceremony and /destination-weddings/weddings-abroad-where-can-you-legally-get-married.
